mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has moved from -34.4 to -30.9 over the last four weeks, indicating a gradual return of commuting activity. This restored commuting pattern feeds adjacent retail and recreation footfall (lunch stops, after-work errands), so RETAIL_REC should continue rising over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise or declines over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing its upward trajectory for three or more consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has drifted down from 10.7 to 8.6 over the snapshot period, reflecting reduced home-confinement behavior. Once RESIDENTIAL falls below a threshold of 8.0, households reallocate freed time toward discretionary outings, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 8.0 percent change from baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks after RESIDENTIAL crosses below the 8.0 threshold.

mechanism_narrative: Both TRANSIT (-45.1 to -41.7) and WORKPLACES (-34.4 to -30.9) show synchronized recovery, suggesting commuting infrastructure usage and office presence are reinforcing each other. When both series trend upward simultaneously, the combined effect on foot traffic near transit hubs and workplaces produces a stronger lift in RETAIL_REC than either series alone would predict.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 28 days is no greater than the growth predicted by WORKPLACES alone, indicating no synergistic interaction between TRANSIT and WORKPLACES recovery.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has remained elevated (44-57 percent above baseline) across the last three weeks, consistent with a warm-season shift toward outdoor leisure. This substitution effect diverts discretionary time away from indoor retail and recreation venues, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth when PARKS stays above 40.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains above 40 percent change from baseline for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks even though PARKS remains above the 40-point threshold throughout that period.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week rebound in TRANSIT usage signals that policy-driven restrictions on public transport and gathering are easing. Such rapid easing historically precedes a near-term surge in retail and recreation visits as consumers test newly reopened venues within a week of the transit uptick.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises more than 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following a TRANSIT week-on-week increase exceeding 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has climbed steadily from -5.3 to 2.0 over the snapshot, indicating normalization of essential-errand behavior. This normalization is an early behavioral signal that spills over quickly into discretionary retail visits, producing a short-horizon uptick in RETAIL_REC within one week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following a positive GROCERY_PHARM reading despite GROCERY_PHARM maintaining its upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous policy-driven workplace reopening (WORKPLACES improving) and reduced mandated home-stay orders (RESIDENTIAL declining) jointly indicate a broader relaxation regime. When both indicators move in the expected direction together, the combined policy signal produces a stronger and more durable rise in RETAIL_REC over four weeks than either indicator alone.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises and RESIDENTIAL falls in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed the trend predicted by WORKPLACES alone during weeks when both WORKPLACES rises and RESIDENTIAL falls simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility pulls back sharply from its recent peak (57.4 at t-2w), the end of a transient outdoor-activity spike would redirect foot traffic back toward indoor retail and recreation venues, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks of the parks decline.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 15 points week-on-week from its recent peak
regime_hint: seasonal transition out of peak outdoor activity
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks of a PARKS week-on-week decline exceeding 15 points.
